chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who runs between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, so he said: 'Yes, by my life, indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Asma' bint 'Umays to perform ghusl, then make up for what she missed, and then perform tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah.'

key_terms.اَلصَّفَا وَ اَلْمَرْوَة: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.اِسْتَثْفَرَتْ: She made up for what she missed (specifically tawaf)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a menstruating woman regarding tawaf during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *tawaf al-ziyarah* for menstruating women by citing the precedent of Asma' bint Umays, who performed ritual bath (*ghusl*) and then proceeded to perform tawaf between Safa and Marwa. It establishes that while menstruation suspends the immediate obligation, it does not invalidate the rite itself, requiring only purification and completion of the circuit. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of Umrah and Hajj rituals when menstruation occurs during the sacred days.
